clue.text: One might be hired and fired the same day!

definitions.text: One might be hired and fired the same day!

parts.words: One might be hired and fired the same day!
parts.note: hired and fired suggests a worker sacked on day one, but this performer is booked for a show and shot out of a gun at it

explanation.surface: A grim joke about a worker taken on in the morning and sacked by evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' looks like dismissal from a job; it is literal, the circus act being launched from a cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus stunt performer is engaged for a show and then propelled from a cannon during it.

clue.text: Move liquid around swimmer in castle environs

parts.note: to stir is to move liquid around with a spoon
the ling is a sea fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a drink around a fish in the grounds of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: STIRLING is a Scottish city clustered around its famous castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish town grew up around the rock of its royal fortress, so it is that stronghold's surroundings.

clue.text: Second taxi for blackleg

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A striker needs another taxi to get past the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blackleg' is British for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are insulting names for a worker who crosses a picket line during a strike.

clue.text: Officer gets supporters positioned round hilltop

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: round says the word for positioned goes around the next piece

parts.note: sat means placed or positioned

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so hill gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: An officer has troops placed around the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hilltop' is split: 'top' picks H from 'hill', which sits inside SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is slang for a senior military officer, after the gold braid on the cap.

clue.text: Crowd needs gold for elaborate cake

parts.note: the gate is the crowd attending a sporting event
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A crowd demands gold in exchange for a fancy cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered French cake with cream or fruit is the sort of showy dessert meant.

clue.text: Mockingbird takes time with hot meat slice

parts.note: H is hot, as on a tap
a rasher is a slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A bird helps itself, taking a moment with a hot slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: These songbirds belong to the mimid family, the same family as mockingbirds, so one is an example.

clue.text: Black companion wrapping small jumper finds jewelled badge

indicators.note: wrapping says the first pieces enclose the jumper

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
CH is Companion of Honour
a roo is a kangaroo, shortened, and kangaroos jump

explanation.surface: A dark-clad friend wraps up a little jumper and finds a pin among its folds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater; it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental pin, often set with stones, worn on clothing like a badge.

clue.text: Bet was placed here, evens, with truth and error recalculated

indicators.note: recalculated says these letters are worked out again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gambler's sum about even-money odds goes wrong and has to be redone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bet Lynch was the landlady of the Rovers Return, the pub in the British TV soap Coronation Street; 'Bet' and 'evens' look like wagering.
explanation.definitionFit: The barmaid character Bet Lynch was installed as landlady of this soap opera pub.

clue.text: The Hives' original song about facial twitch

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original or earliest, as in Ur-text
a tic is an involuntary twitch, often of the face
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A rock band's first single is about a nervous facial twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hives are a Swedish rock band, but here hives is the itchy rash.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for nettle rash, the raised itchy weals commonly called hives.

clue.text: Stuffing rook into pot is cruel

indicators.note: stuffing one thing into another puts it inside

parts.note: pot and hash are both slang for cannabis
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Cramming a bird into a cooking pot is a cruel thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests a cooking pot; it is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and cruel both describe treatment that is severe and unkind.

clue.text: Organisms in bubbly confectionery with lots of cream

parts.note: Aero is a British chocolate bar full of bubbles

indicators.note: lots of a word, not all of it, means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the cream of something is the best of it

explanation.surface: Microbes are found in a bubbly chocolate bar with plenty of cream.
explanation.walkthrough: AERO is a bubbly British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: These are life forms such as bacteria that need oxygen to live.

clue.text: Locks turned by soldiers protecting uniform's charm

indicators.note: turned says the word for locks is read backwards

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair, or locks

indicators.note: protecting means the soldiers surround the next letter

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier's hair is cut by the troops guarding the charm of the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's love or delight them, so to captivate or bewitch.

clue.text: Stylish husband, one going into clubs twice

indicators.note: going into means the husband and one sit inside
twice says the clubs letter appears two times

parts.note: C is clubs in card notation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A smart husband goes to two different nightclubs in one evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone fashionable and elegant in appearance.

clue.text: Red leader and King Henry attack Revolutionary Five

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance
to rush is to charge at or attack
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A monarch and Henry launch an assault on a band of five rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikita, the Soviet premier in the late 1950s and early 1960s, led the communist Soviet Union.

clue.text: Disregard information about displaced Celt

indicators.note: about says the word for information turns round

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: displaced says the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the facts about a Celt forced from his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore or fail to attend to something, the verb sense of both.

clue.text: Say Mrs Tanner drinks no rum to start with, but this is port

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the name swallows the next letters

parts.note: Elsie Tanner was a character in the British TV soap Coronation Street; say marks the name as an example

indicators.note: to start with picks the first letter of rum

explanation.surface: A landlady sips no rum at first, but this is port she has in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsie Tanner was a character in Coronation Street; 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's Danish setting, Helsingør, is a harbour town on the Øresund strait.

clue.text: Horse discards wings in beginning to catch space ship

indicators.note: in says the wingless horse goes inside the next pieces
beginning to picks the opening letter of catch

parts.note: air is the open space above us

indicators.note: discards wings means the word loses its outer letters at each side

explanation.surface: A horse moults its wings while trying to catch a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate vessel of the Barbary coast is the classic vessel of this name.

clue.text: Holiday venue needs quote to install electrical units

indicators.note: to install means to put inside, so the units go into the quote word

parts.note: to cite is to quote
amps are units of electric current

explanation.surface: A holiday resort needs a price quote for installing electrical points.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people pitch tents on vacation, so somewhere to stay on a break.

clue.text: Alpha male with something excellent that would devastate

parts.note: A is alpha, the first Greek letter
a tom is a male cat
in British slang a bomb is a great success, as in going like a bomb

explanation.surface: A dominant man with something superb that could wreck everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpha male' reads as one phrase but splits into A and TOM; British 'a bomb' means a big success.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear weapon is the very thing designed to wreak devastation.

clue.text: Old authors echo identical means to achieve result

parts.note: pens are writers, as in hired pens
E is echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
same means identical

explanation.surface: Old writers repeat the same tried methods to get what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: This is Ali Baba's magic password that opened the robbers' cave.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for any infallible way of gaining access or a desired outcome.

clue.text: Pass close to Awatere Fault

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or fault

explanation.surface: A trip goes near New Zealand's Awatere Fault, a geological fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Awatere Fault is a real New Zealand fault line, but 'Fault' here is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to go by, or slip away, as it passes.

clue.text: Duke and daughter occupy Manchester town land

indicators.note: occupy means the duke and daughter move inside the town

parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and his daughter take over land in a Manchester town.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town near Manchester; 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in land someone with a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden someone with an unwanted task, as in being lumbered with it.

clue.text: Penniless piano player finally gets rounds in

indicators.note: in says the rounds go inside the other letters

parts.note: P is piano, quietly, in music

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of player

parts.note: O is round in shape, so two rounds are two Os

explanation.surface: A broke pianist still manages to buy the drinks at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rounds in' suggests buying drinks, but the rounds are two ring-shaped letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all, the state of being destitute or impoverished.

clue.text: Put into bed, come down with serious head problem

indicators.note: put into means the falling word goes inside bed

parts.note: rain is to come down from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone sent to bed falls ill with a severe headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brained has taken a hard blow to the skull, a grave injury to the head.

clue.text: Instrument once used to fire on vessel coming about

indicators.note: on says the dismissal word comes first, with the next piece put after it

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job

indicators.note: coming about, as a boat turns, says the vessel is read backwards

parts.note: a tub is a vessel, both a container and a slow boat

explanation.surface: A cannon once used to fire on a ship as it turned.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance forerunner of the trombone, an obsolete brass wind instrument.

clue.text: Male lobster seen in lift

definitions.meaning: a male crab or lobster is called by the same name as a male bird
to raise, as one does a hat brim, an ear or a gun's hammer

explanation.surface: A male lobster is spotted inside an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Male crustaceans take the farmyard word, and to raise an ear or eyebrow uses it too.

clue.text: More intimate when leaderless one defeated

indicators.note: leaderless means losing the first letter

parts.note: closer means more intimate

explanation.surface: A more intimate relationship falls apart once the leader goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beaten in a contest is the vanquished party.

clue.text: Perhaps meet Carol — she's turned up after all!

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet Carol, who finally shows up after everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after all' means after everyone else, not 'in the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving after everyone else has got there is a tardy arrival.
